title: Bitewise run sprint log - Lina
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal tracker for the ‘Bitewise’ micro-bench sprint — capture short-run configs, coarse latency/cost numbers, and immediate follow-ups so I don’t lose context between ad-hoc runs. Not polished; use as quick reference when re-running experiments or filing JIRA.

Run summary table (top-level):
run_id | date | model | quant | batch | seq_len | kv_cache | latency_ms_p50 | latency_ms_p95 | tps_tokens | est_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd | notes
BW-001 | 2024-11-02 | rwd-13b-v1 | 8-bit | 1 | 512 | off | 68 | 115 | 520 | 0.012 | baseline, no kv cache, warm cold-cache
BW-002 | 2024-11-03 | rwd-13b-v1 | 8-bit | 4 | 512 | on | 45 | 90 | 780 | 0.009 | kv cache hits ~65%, batching helps latency
BW-003 | 2024-11-07 | rwd-13b-q4 | q4_0 | 4 | 1024 | on | 72 | 140 | 1200 | 0.0065 | larger seq len, tail latency increases
BW-004 | 2024-12-10 | rwd-13b-q4 | q4_0 | 8 | 256 | on | 38 | 80 | 1600 | 0.0058 | aggressive batching, watch memory spill
BW-005 | 2025-01-10 | rwd-70b-v1 | 16-bit | 1 | 2048 | off | 230 | 410 | 640 | 0.045 | exploratory, single-threaded, high variance

Key observations (raw notes):
- KV cache gave consistent p50 wins (~25-35% lower) on steady traffic. Best impact when prompt prefix stable across requests.
- Batching >4 starts to give diminishing returns for low-seq workloads (<512). For 2048 seq length, batching helps throughput but increases p95.
- q4 quant worked well on 13b for cost tradeoffs; watch hallucination rate on longer-generated outputs (qual check needed).
- Memory: on rwd-70b with 16-bit, background processes can push GPU memory to spill — add quick check before big runs (nvidia-smi snapshot).

Quick quality checklist (manual)
- [ ] run human quality spot-check for BW-003 outputs (prompt subset A)
- [x] sanity-check token accounting against billing logs for BW-001..BW-004
- [ ] annotate where reranking changes output ordering for prompt set B

Immediate action items (next time I run):
1) Add consistent seed param to runs (I forgot for BW-002 and BW-003) – need reproducibility.
2) For q4 quant tests, attach the eval prompt subset and diff against 8-bit baseline (JIRA-ENG-7891).
3) Create tiny script to capture GPU mem + nvtop snapshot and auto-upload with run metadata.
4) Re-run BW-004 with batch=12 and measure server-side queueing (observe p95).

Notes to self about logging format:
- Keep run_id prefix BW-<NNN> so grep is trivial.
- Minimal required fields: model, quant, batch, seq_len, kv_cache, latency_p50/p95, tps_tokens, cost_est.
- Save a tiny JSON metadata file alongside outputs (date, hostname, git-sha).

Context links and where this came from:
- Started after pairing with Arjun on 2024-11-01 — wanted smaller bite-sized runs to iterate faster.
- See PR above for reproducible-run harness (links in linked_artifacts).

Open questions / things to investigate later:
- How much of p95 tail for 13b is network vs scheduling? Need traces (x-trace) from console.
- For private deployments: is the KV cache warm-up pattern different due to NFS latency? quick A/B test needed on private cluster.
- Should we try per-route fallback to 8-bit q4_0 for specific prompt sets rather than global policy?

Random scribbles (for later cleanup):
- idea: prefix-hash TTL on KV cache, evict small prefixes to keep hit-rate high for common prompts.
- note: when batching >12 observed occasional 500-levels (maybe batching overflow) — add retry/backoff in harness.

End of sprint scratchpad. Keep this file short-lived; if anything is worth keeping, I’ll promote to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/ and link from the JIRA ticket.
